newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Fall in T-bill yields reflects Russian economy.
newsitem.headline: Fall in T-bill yields reflects Russian economy.

text.p: A fall in yields on long-term issues of Russian GKO discount Treasury bills reflects changes in the Russian economy, First Deputy Central Bank Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said on Tuesday.

"Our financial circles are re-evaluating the situation and the (yield) levels which were considered normal three months ago are now extremely high," Aleksashenko told Reuters. "Banks understand it is impossible to count on super-profitability."
Aleksashenko said Russian demand dominated the market, while an inflow of funds from foreign investors had stabilised.

"There is an inflow of funds from non-residents, it is a stable stream, although not as strong as in winter," he said. "The balance of foreign investment in May is about $1 billion, in April it was a little over $1 billion."

Russian government and Central Bank officials say T-bill yields will fall to 20 percent annual by the end of the year. On Monday the average yield fell to 23.2 percent from 23.6 percent on Friday. In February the yields were between 25 and 30 percent.

"We are sure the yield by the year-end will be around 20 percent, but our goal is a fall in the yield to 0.5 percent above inflation rate," Aleksashenko said. "We understand the market can offer resistance, but there is no fear it will be significant." Inflation is forecast at 12 percent this year after 22 percent in 1996.
